ideas.description: Exploit: spend E053's margin on the two time cuts already measured as accuracy-neutral on dev seeds. On E053 (E038 + head output scale 2x, ls 0.4; official 0.7575, dev 0.7578 @ 6.68 s), make two changes. (1) The pooling cut: replace the head's AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) with x.flatten(2).max(dim=2).values at every resolution and in eval. Use the indices-based backward, not amax (amax crashed in E041). (2) E049's 2-epoch whitening-bias window: train the whitening-conv bias only in the 20 px phase, and in the 24 px graph detach the whitening output after its activation and zero the bias lr. Keep the graph count at 4, recapture everything in build, and change nothing else. Check that eval returns finite [B,100] logits for B in {1, 7, 513, 1024}. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12.
ideas.expected: Time about 6.42-6.46 s (-3.3 to -3.9%: pooling -0.19 s, bias window -0.06 s; E049 measured 6.45 s for the same pair). Both cuts remove work, so the gain should carry over to the PCIe judge. Dev 10-seed mean about 0.7565 (range 0.754-0.759): the cuts measured -0.09 and -0.04 pp on dev, against E053's 0.7578. Keep if official >=0.7535 and dev >=0.754. If dev falls >=0.25 pp below E053, the scale-2x gain interacts with the max-pool gradient routing; then re-test the pooling cut alone.

ideas.description: Exploit, the next banked cut, stacked on the current tip (idea A's stack if kept, else E053). Move one 32 px epoch to 28 px, giving 2x20+3x24+3x28+3x32: 11 epochs, the LR triangle and Lookahead over total steps, the same 4 graphs. The 28 px graph keeps conv1 trainable, as now (E050 showed conv1 needs its 28 px updates). Change nothing else. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12, and compare against the tip's own dev mean.
ideas.expected: Time -0.09 to -0.11 s (E037 measured -0.10 s), about 6.33-6.36 s on A's stack. Dev mean -0.0 to -0.25 pp vs the tip, centred near -0.1 pp. Keep if dev >=0.754 and official >=0.7535. A dev drop <=0.1 pp supports H2.3.2 (the closing 32 px phase mostly re-fits to the test resolution), and 2x28+... toward a 2x32 tail becomes the next probe. A drop >=0.3 pp means the 32 px phase is doing feature learning: refute H2.3.2 and close the ladder.

ideas.description: Explore, continuing the only margin source found since E030. On the current tip (A's stack if kept, else E053), raise the head's fixed output scale from 2x to 3x the original airbench-derived value. ls stays 0.4 and nothing else changes. The scale is a graph constant, so recapture all graphs in build. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12. Contingency: if dev rises >=0.15 pp, try 4x next. If it falls >=0.15 pp, 2x is near the optimum; then test ls 0.3 at 2x scale, since the scale and ls interact.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Dev mean -0.3 to +0.3 pp vs the tip, weak prior +0.05 to +0.15 pp: 1x→2x gave +0.44 pp, so the optimum likely sits at or above 2x but the response must flatten. Keep if dev gain >=0.1 pp and official >=0.7535. A gain would add margin to spend on the tail trim and group-2 cut.

ideas.description: Exploit, and measure the tail slope in the cheap direction now that margin exists. On the current tip, cut the 32 px phase from 4 to 3.5 epochs (16 fewer steps at batch 1536 with drop_last). Keep the LR triangle and Lookahead over total steps, as in E032, which added the same half-epoch. Change nothing else; no new graphs. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12. E032's +0.5 epoch at 32 px bought -0.06 pp on one draw, so the tail may be saturated and a trim could be cheap.
ideas.expected: Time -0.32 to -0.38 s (about -5%). Dev mean -0.1 to -0.45 pp vs the tip, centred near -0.25 pp. Keep if dev >=0.754 and official >=0.7535; the -5% would beat any other banked cut. A dev drop <=0.15 pp means the 32 px tail is saturated (the H6/plateau reading gains, and margin should go to tail trims). A drop >=0.4 pp means the tail is ~1 pp/epoch: stop trimming epochs and spend margin only on per-step cuts.

ideas.description: Exploit, a work-removal cut in group 2 that has not yet been tried. First microbenchmark ms/step per phase on the current recipe (graphed, Muon included) for group 2 at 3 vs 2 convs. If the 2-conv version saves >=3% ms/step, cut group 2 from 3 convs to 2 (net 2/2/3) at the same width 384, keeping the pooling position, and adjust the Muon batched-NS shape groups. Hold epochs, resolutions, schedule, ls, head scale, freezing and the bias window fixed. Recapture all graphs in build. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12. If the microbenchmark saves <2%, log it and do not run.
ideas.expected: Time -3 to -5% (about -0.2 to -0.3 s), including Muon NS savings from one fewer 384x3456 filter matrix. Dev mean -0.15 to -0.6 pp, centred near -0.3 pp (group-1's first depth cut cost 0.29 pp in E009). Keep if dev >=0.754 and official >=0.7535. If the cost is <=0.3 pp for >=4% time, this beats the epoch line, and H6.1.4 (2 convs at 512) becomes the follow-up to buy the accuracy back.

ideas.description: Explore, a diagnostic only, run outside the official command and the timed region, with no recipe change. After training on dev seeds 3-7 (5 trials), compute un-augmented top-1 accuracy and mean loss on a fixed 10k training subset (drawn with a fixed generator) for two configs: the current tip and E038 (head scale 1x). Test accuracy is logged as usual. Nothing is kept. This tells us whether the head-scale gain came from better fit or less over-regularization, and whether the recipe under-fits (margin from steps or capacity) or has a large gap (margin from regularization).
ideas.expected: Metrics unchanged (no submission change). Prediction: tip train accuracy in [0.82, 0.92], train-test gap <=15 pp, and the 2x scale raises train accuracy by at least its +0.44 pp test gain. Train accuracy >=0.95 refutes H7.1 and moves margin work to regularization (jitter H1.3.5, flip H1.2, ls form). Train accuracy <0.85 supports capacity and anchor-fixed steps (H1.8.2, H6.1).

ideas.description: Exploit, numerically near-equivalent work removal in Muon. First check the AOL code. If the column scaling computes X^T X and the first NS step then recomputes the Gram matrix, reuse it as A1 = s·A0·s (Turbo-Muon Algorithm 2), removing one large matmul per parameter group per step inside the batched NS call. If the reuse is already present, close H2.5.5 without a run. Otherwise change nothing else, recapture all graphs in build, and run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12.
ideas.expected: Muon GPU time -0.1 to -0.2 ms/step over about 350 steps, so time -0.04 to -0.07 s (-0.6 to -1%). Dev mean within ±0.1 pp of the tip (same math up to fp16 rounding). Keep if time is >=0.5% lower, dev >=0.754 and official >=0.7535. This is removed FLOPs, so it should carry over to the judge.

structured_output.summary:
E053's head scale (2x) is the first real margin source since E030, worth about +0.44 pp on dev seeds (0.7578), so the loop changes from finding margin to spending it. Seven new ideas are queued, alongside I060, which is still running.

**Exploit (spend the margin, in order):**
- **A, priority 5:** stack the two cuts already measured as neutral on dev seeds, the pooling change and the 2-epoch whitening-bias window. Expected about 6.44 s, with dev around 0.7565.
- **Priority 4:** add the 28 px tail shift (H2.3.2), another -0.10 s.
- **Priority 3:** cut the 32 px tail by half an epoch (H1.8), about -0.35 s. This also measures how much the tail is worth: E032 suggested it may be saturated.
- **Priority 3:** cut group 2 from 3 convs to 2, behind a microbenchmark gate (H2.4.7).
- **Priority 2:** reuse the Gram matrix in Muon's Newton-Schulz step (H2.5.5). This needs a code check first.

**Explore:**
- **Priority 4:** probe head scale 3x (H1.3.4). The scale is still the most promising free knob.
- **Priority 2:** a dev-only diagnostic of how well the model fits the training set (H7.1.1). It decides whether further margin should come from capacity and more steps or from regularization.

Every keep needs the dev 10-seed mean at or above 0.754 and the official run at or above 0.7535, so no passing draw is selected by chance. Nothing is dropped: all earlier queued ideas are done or already dropped, and I060 is in progress.
